title: util-review customization contract
description: Every placeholder the util-review templates (SKILL.md.tmpl + references/check-catalog.md.tmpl) expose. A profile supplies a value for each. util-review's customization axis is HOST PORTABILITY, not org-binding: the `public` profile renders host-neutral prose (Agent Skills / AGENTS.md / 'a host agent' — ships to the marketplace, works across providers); the `matt-local` profile renders Claude-Code-specific prose (CLAUDE.md / 'Claude' / disable-model-invocation / ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} / Opus-Sonnet-Haiku). None of util-review's tokens are the spine globals (owner/tracker/chat) — they do not appear in this skill. render_skill.py validates that the templates' placeholders and a profile's keys agree.

desc.description: SKILL.md frontmatter description string. Host-neutral lists 'Agent Skills … AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md … any supplementary agent artifact'; local says 'Claude Code skills … CLAUDE.md … any supplementary Claude Code artifact'.
examples: Review Agent Skills, hooks, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md files, scripts, MCP configs, or workflow configurations for design flaws, unclosed loops, stale references, side effects, security risks, and portability issues. Use when: 'review this skill', 'audit this hook', '/util-review', 'check this config', or when evaluating any supplementary agent artifact for quality and correctness.

Review Claude Code skills, hooks, CLAUDE.md files, scripts, or workflow configurations for design flaws, unclosed loops, stale references, side effects, security risks, and portability issues. Use when: 'review this skill', 'audit this hook', '/util-review', 'check this config', or when evaluating any supplementary Claude Code artifact for quality and correctness.

overview_body.description: The Overview paragraph. Public form is hard-wrapped and names 'supplementary agent artifacts'; local form is single-line and names 'Claude Code supplementary artifacts'.
examples:
Perform a deep, systematic review of supplementary agent artifacts — Agent
Skills, hooks, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md files, scripts, MCP configurations, or
workflow definitions. Surfaces design flaws, unclosed loops, incorrect
references, stale assumptions, side effects, security risks, portability issues,
and unanswered design questions that structural validators miss.

Perform a deep, systematic review of Claude Code supplementary artifacts — skills, hooks, CLAUDE.md files, scripts, MCP configurations, or workflow definitions. Surfaces design flaws, unclosed loops, incorrect references, stale assumptions, side effects, security risks, portability issues, and unanswered design questions that structural validators miss.

s_applies.description: 'Applies To' cell for the Structure & Format row in the coverage table.
examples: Skills, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md
Skills, CLAUDE.md

artifact_md_bullet.description: Phase 1 artifact-detection bullet for the instruction-file type. Public covers AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md with generic imports; local is CLAUDE.md with `@import`.
examples: **AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md**: instruction files — check for imports or linked references and read those too
**CLAUDE.md**: Instruction file — check for `@import` references and read those too

audience_tail.description: Tail of the Phase 2 'Who is the audience?' line after 'Human users? '. Public says 'Host agent auto-invocation? … Delegated agents?'; local says 'Claude (auto-invocation)? … Sub-agents?'.
examples: Host agent auto-invocation? Both? Delegated agents?
Claude (auto-invocation)? Both? Sub-agents?

reg_both.description: Registration outcome for the both-human-and-model case.
examples: default host-discoverable metadata
default (no flags)

reg_human_only.description: Registration outcome for the human-only case. Local cites the concrete `disable-model-invocation: true` flag.
examples: use the host's supported human-invocation flag or adapter metadata
`disable-model-invocation: true`

reg_machine_only.description: Registration outcome for the machine-only case. Local cites the concrete `user-invocable: false` flag.
examples: use the host's supported model-invocation flag or adapter metadata
`user-invocable: false`

discovery_viable.description: Phase 2 'Is discovery viable?' body. Local names Claude's matcher and the concrete first-250-character truncation point.
examples: Will a host agent's description-matching find this when relevant? Are trigger keywords present? Is the key use case early in the description?
Will Claude's description-matching find this when relevant? Are trigger keywords present? Is the key use case in the first 250 characters (truncation point)?

d001_summary_tail.description: Phase 3 D001 summary-table tail. Public resolves bundled paths relative to the active SKILL.md; local uses `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`.
examples: resolve portable resources relative to the active `SKILL.md`, not hardcoded absolute paths
use `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` for portability, not hardcoded absolute paths

r003_summary_tail.description: Phase 3 R003 summary-table tail after 'Instructions work across '. Public is model-tier-neutral; local names Opus/Sonnet/Haiku.
examples: model capability tiers without vendor/model-specific assumptions
Claude models (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) without model-specific assumptions

g004_summary_tail.description: Phase 3 G004 summary-table tail after 'User interaction quality — '. Local names AskUserQuestion with concrete limits.
examples: structured clarification asks few questions with clear options when the host supports it
AskUserQuestion uses 1-4 questions, 2-4 options, ≤12-char headers

notes_hook.description: Notes bullet on hook-review version sensitivity. Public is host/version-generic (hard-wrapped); local pins the Claude Code `if` field to v2.1.85+.
examples:
For hook reviews, behavior differs by host and version. Check the adapter docs
  for the exact event schema.
For hook reviews, behavior can differ between Claude Code versions. The `if` field requires v2.1.85+.

notes_fork.description: Notes bullet on isolated-context skills. Public says 'isolated/delegated context … the delegated agent' (hard-wrapped); local says '`context: fork` … the sub-agent'.
examples:
Skills using isolated/delegated context must provide enough actionable context
  for the delegated agent to produce useful output — guidelines alone without a
  task prompt return nothing.
Skills using `context: fork` must provide enough actionable context for the sub-agent to produce useful output — guidelines alone without a task prompt return nothing.

m001_rationale.description: check-catalog M001 rationale. Public: 'many hosts; some ignore the frontmatter…'; local: 'Claude Code won't error — it'll just ignore…'.
examples:
Invalid YAML silently breaks skill loading in many hosts; some ignore
the frontmatter and treat the entire file as body content.
Invalid YAML silently breaks skill loading. Claude Code won't error — it'll just ignore the frontmatter and treat the entire file as body content.

examples:
The description is the #1 failure point for auto-discovery. Host
agents use it to decide relevance. Vague descriptions = never invoked.
The description is the #1 failure point for auto-discovery. Claude uses it to decide relevance. Vague descriptions = never invoked.

d001_look.description: check-catalog D001 what-to-look-for. Public: 'Host-neutral paths … relative to the active SKILL.md'; local: '`${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` for bundled files'.

r003_rationale.description: check-catalog R003 rationale. Public: 'a high-capability model … a smaller model'; local: 'Opus … Haiku'.

examples:
Reliance on capabilities that vary across models (complex
reasoning, long context, tool use patterns). Consider whether the skill specifies
a model or will be used across models.
Reliance on capabilities that vary across models (complex reasoning, long context, tool use patterns). Consider whether the skill specifies a model or will be used across models.

g002_look.description: check-catalog G002 what-to-look-for. Public: 'Structured user clarification?'; local: 'AskUserQuestion?'.
examples:
How does the artifact get each piece of required context?
Structured user clarification? File reads? Tool calls? Environment variables? Is
each strategy appropriate for its data?
How does the artifact get each piece of required context? AskUserQuestion? File reads? Tool calls? Environment variables? Is each strategy appropriate for its data?

g004_look.description: check-catalog G004 what-to-look-for. Public: generic 'A small number of questions … when the host supports structured choices'; local: concrete AskUserQuestion limits.
examples:
A small number of questions per interaction. When the host
supports structured choices, options are mutually exclusive and collectively
exhaustive.
AskUserQuestion with 1-4 questions per interaction. 2-4 options per question. Headers ≤12 characters. Options are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive.

h004_rationale.description: check-catalog H004 rationale. Public: 'a stop hook that always returns the host's continue/interrupt code … the agent'; local: 'a Stop hook that always exits 2 … Claude'.
examples: A stop hook that always returns the host's continue/interrupt code creates an infinite loop — the agent can never finish responding.
A Stop hook that always exits 2 creates an infinite loop — Claude can never finish responding.
